rules: This is a PowerShell IT Helpdesk Toolkit with 253 tools in 20 categories. It has two UIs: console (HelpdeskToolkit.ps1) and GUI (HelpdeskToolkit-GUI.ps1). Both load the same tool definitions from Modules/. Fully portable for flash drives.

The tool system uses Add-Tool function (defined in Core/Common.ps1) to register tools. Every tool must have: Id (e.g., NET-02), Category, Name, Description, Action script block, and optional Admin flag.
Tool files are in Toolkit/Modules/ numbered 01-21 (one per category). File order = menu order. New category = new file like 22-CategoryName.ps1.

When adding/modifying tools: edit Toolkit/Modules/NN-Category.ps1, test in console first (./Toolkit/HelpdeskToolkit.ps1), then GUI (./Toolkit/HelpdeskToolkit-GUI.ps1), then rebuild (./Toolkit/Build-SingleFile.ps1).
Tools use Write-Host, Write-Info, Write-Ok, Write-Err, Write-Section, Write-Check for output (all support color). Read-Host, Confirm-Action, Select-FromList auto-convert to GUI dialogs.

GUI settings and favorites are stored in Toolkit/Settings/ folder (portable with toolkit). Output goes to Documents/HelpdeskToolkit/ folder (logs, reports, case files). Get-OutFile -Name 'file.csv' returns the full path with timestamp.
Build-SingleFile.ps1 creates dist/ with two standalone copies. It syntax-checks all modules first and stops on error. Always rebuild after editing modules before testing dist/.
Admin-only tools are marked -Admin in Add-Tool and stay greyed out in GUI until user elevates. Console skips them when not admin.
Every destructive action must ask Confirm-Action first (delete, reset, uninstall, log off). Read-only tools can run silently.
Module errors don't crash the toolkit—they're skipped with a warning and logged. Other tools still work.
The GUI runs tools in a background runspace via GuiHost.ps1 so the window never freezes. Long jobs show progress and can be stopped.
After ANY module change: (1) test console, (2) test GUI, (3) test single tool via -Run, (4) rebuild dist/, (5) test one tool in dist/, (6) commit & push.
Use git feature branches: git checkout -b feature/your-feature, test locally, then merge back to main and push.
All paths use $PSScriptRoot and relative paths for portability. No hardcoded drive letters or APPDATA paths.
